claims.text: As-received Q235 steel has a native oxide film.
As-received Q235 steel contains inherent MnS inclusions.
MnS inclusions in Q235 steel act as localized anodic sites that initiate pitting corrosion.
Localized acid cleaning and mechanical polishing will remove or reduce surface MnS inclusions.
Controlled re-passivation will restore a uniform native oxide film after acid cleaning and polishing.
Surface MnS inclusion density governs the formation of local micro-galvanic cells.
MnS inclusions preferentially dissolve in chloride-containing environments.
Dissolution associated with MnS inclusions forms localized galvanic couples that accelerate pitting corrosion.
Reducing MnS inclusion density minimizes local micro-galvanic cells.
Minimizing MnS-associated micro-galvanic cells delays corrosion initiation and propagation.
Re-passivation makes corrosion differences attributable to inclusion density rather than to changes in the protective oxide film.
Inclusion-reduced specimens will have lower pit density than untreated Q235 at approximately 25 °C and 60 °C in chloride solution.
Inclusion-reduced specimens will have lower mass loss than untreated Q235 at approximately 25 °C and 60 °C in chloride solution.
Inclusion-reduced specimens with a restored oxide film will have higher electrochemical impedance than untreated Q235 at approximately 25 °C and 60 °C.
Changes in bulk composition and other microstructural variables are negligible in the proposed controlled study.

contradictions.description: The study is said to vary only MnS inclusion density, but the treated group also receives acid cleaning, mechanical polishing, and re-passivation while the untreated control does not. These operations can alter surface roughness, residual stress, near-surface microstructure, and oxide state, so the stated single-variable isolation is not ensured by the described design.
